newsitem.title: USA: Bankruptcy judge rejects implant claim proposals.
newsitem.headline: Bankruptcy judge rejects implant claim proposals.

text.p: A federal bankruptcy judge Wednesday rejected proposals from both Dow Corning Corp. and breast implant plaintiffs over how to value personal injury claims against the company.

U.S. Bankruptcy Court Judge Arthur Spector said Dow Corning should resubmit a Chapter 11 reorganization plan by Aug. 20 on which both sides agree on how much to pay plaintiffs, said Dow Corning spokesman Michael Jackson.

The company, facing lawsuits from tens of thousands of women, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy court protection two years ago. Women allege the silicone gel breast implants once made by the Midland, Mich.-based firm cause numerous health problems such as connective tissue diseases.
Dow Corning denies the claims. The company is a joint venture of Dow Chemical Co. and Corning Inc..

If the two sides cannot agree on a damage estimate, Spector said he would recommend to a federal district court that a separate "causation" trial be held with a panel of experts to determine whether silicone breast implants can cause health problems, said Jackson.
Dow Corning claimed a victory because Spector endorsed the idea of a causation trial over plaintiff proposals for a number of summary trials involving real plaintiffs.

"We believe it is a mistake not to go immediately to a range of sample trials," said Ralph Knowles, a member of the tort claimants committee, adding that would allow for a more diverse sampling of health problems.
Plaintiffs noted that Spector denied a Dow Corning request to appoint a science panel under his supervision. A similar panel already exists in federal court in Alabama.
